page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 CPU family running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage. It delivers a high-speed baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the average tier for multi-core operations, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48563.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11689.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 973.0 and a gzip compression throughput of 20.34 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show strong cached read speeds of 1894.04 GB/sec, though uncached write speeds drop to 74.98 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates solid capabilities in database operations, achieving 38.79 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and an average Passmark database score of 20432.0.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64-based Graviton architecture provides a resource-dense compute profile with dedicated physical cores, avoiding the overhead of simultaneous multithreading. This makes it highly suitable for scale-out workloads. The high network throughput of 50 Gbps combined with its compute density makes the c6gn.8xlarge well-suited for network-intensive applications, static web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and distributed database workloads.
